html:
Kuwaiti women won the right to vote and stand for parliament in May 2005, when the National Assembly passed a law the government had pushed for years.

Women had campaigned since the 1970s and had played a large part in the resistance during the Iraqi occupation. In 1999 the emir decreed women's suffrage, but the assembly, where Islamist and tribal members were strong, voted it down. The 2005 law passed with government support.

Women first voted in 2006, and four were elected to the assembly in 2009. It was a turning point for the Kuwaiti parliament, and it came years before Saudi women could vote in local elections or drive.
sum: Kuwaiti women won the right to vote and stand for parliament in May 2005, when the National Assembly passed a law the government had pushed for years.
